mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 0.3% in a month coincides with a decline in FEDFUNDS, signaling the Federal Reserve's shift from tightening to holding policy steady, which lowers real discount rates and boosts equity present-value pricing, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 0.3% while FEDFUNDS declines over the preceding month
regime_hint: late-cycle inflation flare-up before rate pause
failure_condition: Over 60-day rolling window, 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than during pre-flare-up periods (Granger causality fails, p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in monthly PAYEMS (labor market strength) above 130,000 coinciding with UNRATE below 5%, suggests robust labor demand and low unemployment, which elevates corporate earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 130,000 for three consecutive months and UNRATE < 5% for the same horizon
regime_hint: labor market strengthening in early recovery phase
failure_condition: In regimes with high structural unemployment, 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than during comparable labor-weak periods (bootstrap CI includes zero).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in GDPC1 (goods orders) exceeding 5% year-over-year, coupled with a decline in RSAFS (retail sales), indicates robust industrial demand while consumer spending remains subdued, which elevates sector-specific optimism in the S&P 500 and produces positive 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY growth > 5% and RSAFS monthly decline over prior month
regime_hint: industrial cycle acceleration in consumer-stagnant phase
failure_condition: Over 100 observations, the Granger causality from GDPC1 to SPX 20d returns is rejected (p > 0.05), or RSAFS decline is not predictive of SPX returns in out-of-sample tests.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly drop in INDPRO (industrial production index) below 95, combined with a rising HOUST (housing starts), signals supply-side softness in manufacturing while housing remains resilient, which can lower growth expectations and produce negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls below 95 and HOUST rises above prior month's level
regime_hint: industrial contraction during housing expansion phase
failure_condition: In 100 out-of-sample windows, 20-day forward returns are not significantly different from a baseline of neutral supply shock (bootstrap p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains above 4.5% for two consecutive months in a period of rising UNRATE (> 7%), it signals persistent tightness in credit conditions, which compresses discount rates and dampens equity valuation growth, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for two consecutive months and UNRATE > 7% for the same horizon
failure_condition: Over 200 episodes, 60-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during comparable high-UNRATE, low-FEDFUNDS regimes (bootstrap p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A one-time monthly spike in PAYEMS above 140,000 accompanied by a sharp drop in UNRATE below 4%, suggests a sudden labor market loosening that boosts hiring expectations and corporate optimism, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns within the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS crosses above 140,000 and UNRATE falls below 4% in the same month
failure_condition: Across 50 such spikes, 5-day forward returns are not significantly higher than during baseline labor-weak periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in INDPRO of at least 2% for three consecutive months, with no offsetting rise in HOUST, indicates ongoing industrial softness and weak manufacturing momentum, which lowers growth forecasts and yields negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines by >= 2% for three consecutive months and HOUST does not recover over the same horizon
failure_condition: In 200 such episodes, the 20-day forward return is not significantly lower than during neutral supply shocks (bootstrap p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in CPIAUCSL below 2% for two consecutive months while FEDFUNDS remains unchanged, signals deflationary pressure without policy easing, which can reduce real discount rates and produce positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls below 2% for two consecutive months and FEDFUNDS unchanged for the same horizon
regime_hint: deflationary pressure in a hold policy regime
failure_condition: Over 150 windows, 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than during comparable inflation-recession periods (Granger causality fails, p > 0.05).
